items.followUp: Use Newton’s second law to find the force needed to accelerate a 4 kg body at 3 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Checks the statement of Newton’s second law, including the direction of the force.
rubric.description: The rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force and occurs in the direction of that force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the law is stated with proportionality and direction.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical form obtained from the momentum change.
rubric.description: The law gives F = Δp/Δt, and for constant mass this becomes F = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mathematical form; accept F = ma or a correct equivalent derivation.

rubric.why: Checks the substitution that identifies the unit force as one newton.
rubric.description: For m = 1 kg and a = 1 m s⁻², F = 1 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly relating 1 kg × 1 m s⁻² to 1 N.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of the SI unit of force in words.
rubric.description: One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition with both the mass and acceleration specified.

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
F ∝ rate of change of momentum.
F = k × change in momentum/time, where k is a proportionality constant.
In SI units, k = 1; therefore, F = change in momentum/time = Δp/Δt.
For a body of mass m changing velocity from u to v in time t:
For m = 1 kg and a = 1 m/s², F = 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 N.
Thus, one newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s²; 1 N = 1 kg m/s².
